sections.content:
The periphrasis **acabar de + infinitivo** expresses that an action was completed just moments before the moment of speaking.

• **Present indicative**: *Acabo de llegar.* (I have just arrived / I just arrived.)
• **Imperfect indicative**: *Acababa de salir cuando me llamaste.* (I had just left when you called me.)
• Unlike English 'just', no adverb is needed — the verb *acabar* followed by *de* encodes immediate recency.

items.spanish: Acabo de recibir un correo electrónico urgente.
items.english: I have just received an urgent email.
Did you just arrive from your trip?

items.spanish: Acabábamos de cenar cuando tocaron al timbre.
items.english: We had just had dinner when the doorbell rang.

sections.content: Always use the infinitive after *de*: *acabo de hablar*, never *acabo de hablado*.
